unattendedProbe.command: codex exec -C "<home>/Code" -s read-only --json --ephemeral "回复 OK，不要做任何别的事。"
unattendedProbe.purpose: record what actually happens under the current (untrusted-new-hooks) state, independent of whether the two new hooks fire
unattendedProbe.result: the turn did not complete: it failed at the model layer with an unrelated error ("The 'gpt-6-astra' model requires a newer version of Codex", HTTP 400) before producing any assistant response. Run exactly once, not retried, per this Story's instruction not to retry or route around a prompt. This failure is orthogonal to hook trust — it is the account's configured default model outrunning the installed 0.148.0 binary (doctor also reports 0.153.4 available) — but it does mean this probe run answers only the hookStartedEventCounts question below, and answers it independent of whether the new hooks are trusted.

storyEvidence.probeOutcome: turn.failed on a model-version error unrelated to hooks; see unattendedProbe.result

hookStartedEventCounts.note: grep -o '"method":"hook/[a-z]*"' found no lines at all in this probe's output, not merely zero after subtracting a nonzero count. The full set of distinct "type" values seen in the run was thread.started, item.completed, turn.started, error, turn.failed — no hook-shaped event type appears anywhere in `codex exec --json`'s event stream. The 0.139.0 survey's own hook/started counts (docs/verification/host/observe-hook-live-acceptance-2026-07-25.json) were measured over a direct App Server JSON-RPC connection, a different transport than `codex exec --json` prints to stdout. So this run cannot distinguish 'the new hooks did not fire because they are untrusted' from 'hook lifecycle events are simply not surfaced on this transport regardless of trust' — both produce the same zero count, and this Story did not have a way to tell them apart without either interactive hook-trust approval or a direct App Server connection, neither of which was available unattended.

unattendedProbe.stdinNote: 0.153.4's `codex exec` waits on stdin even when the prompt is an argument. The first attempt sat on "Reading additional input from stdin..." and had to be killed; redirecting stdin from /dev/null is what makes the command unattended.
unattendedProbe.result: the turn did not complete: HTTP 400, invalid_request_error, "The 'gpt-5.5-mini' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account." No other model was tried, because MIN-141 D1 authorises no other model for tests. This failure is again at the model layer and again orthogonal to hook trust, but it is a different failure than STORY-357's: that one was the account's default model outrunning the installed binary, this one is the authorised test model being unavailable to a ChatGPT-account-backed Codex.

verdictOnTheStopCountCriterion.criterion: ownerActionToClose.afterApproval: a Stop count of 2 confirms the primary STORY-357 design; a count of 1 means the fallback design is required
verdictOnTheStopCountCriterion.verdict: UNRESOLVED: neither 2 nor 1. Zero is this transport's floor rather than a count of how many Stop groups fired, so it selects neither design. Settling it needs both the transport the 0.139.0 survey used (a direct App Server JSON-RPC connection, which surfaces hook lifecycle events) and a model this account may actually run; neither was available to this work item.
verdictOnTheStopCountCriterion.consequence: the fallback rewrite of tools/stop-pact/codex-executor.mjs, tests/host-harness.test.mjs and tests/codex-stop-pact.test.mjs is not triggered by this run, and the primary design is not confirmed by it either. STORY-357's live-fire question stays open.
